summary.heading: Current state
summary.text: GDP holds up at about +0.2–0.3% q/q in Q4 (own estimate, 4 Nov note, unchanged 11 Nov). The Q3 flash was +0.4% q/q (Eurostat, V, 30 Oct); underlying growth excluding Ireland is softer at 0.21 (d). Headline HICP is past the oil peak: the own Q4 view is about 3.8–3.9% y/y (pending; the baseline remains about 4.0), above the September MPE Q4 peak of 3.6, and core shows no second-round signal so far (HICPX October flash 2.5%, V; German CPI core 2.1, U). Deposit facility rate 2.50%. Staff view, not the Governing Council’s or ECB staff projections.
summary.source: ECB Staff Desk note, 12 Nov 2026 (data cut-off 11 Nov, 17:55 CET)

staff_view.lead: Bottom line from the 12 Nov note: growth about +0.2–0.3% q/q in Q4 (own estimate); headline inflation past the oil peak, with a pending own Q4 view of about 3.8–3.9% against a baseline still around 4.0, and no second-round core signal so far.
bullets: Growth: Q3 flash 0.4% (V) is flattered by Ireland (ex-Ireland 0.21, d). Staff Q4 is +0.2–0.3 (own estimate). September retail volume was weak.

Inflation: October HICP flash 4.0% (V) sits above the September MPE Q4 peak of 3.6. The pending own Q4 view (~3.8–3.9) has not replaced the ~4.0 baseline. HICPX 2.5% (V) and German CPI core 2.1 (U) show no second-round signal so far.
Wages and expectations: ECB wage tracker easing into 2027 (V, 6 Nov). CES September: 1y 3.1 / 3y 2.9 / 5y 2.5 (V).
Energy: Brent and TTF quotes on 11 Nov were slightly higher than the 10 Nov references (U, delayed secondary).
Coverage gap: national activity data and surveys from 5–11 Nov are not in the Staff Desk files.
staff_view.policy: Deposit facility rate 2.50%. Inflation outlook: above the September MPE near term, energy-driven, risks balanced to slightly up medium term. charts.title: Euro-area HICP nowcast vs actual — pseudo out-of-sample backtest
charts.subtitle: Staff inflation-nowcast model, current vintage (not real-time). Full sample shown (February 2023–October 2026, n=45). This is the model’s historical error, not a track record of the staff-judgment nowcasts in the table above.
charts.caption: Source: staff inflation-nowcast model, already-produced pseudo out-of-sample backtest (current vintage, not real-time). As of 6 Nov 2026, 10:46 Europe/Zurich (report timestamp 2026-11-06T09:46:12Z). Actuals: Eurostat HICP, current vintage, non-seasonally adjusted, percent month-on-month. The chart is drawn from the already-produced step file; RMSE, MAE and related figures are taken from the already-produced backtest report (same rounding) and its summary JSON. No new model was estimated. Euro-area I25 history is short; the sample starts in 2023. Headline, core and food use a deseasonalised AR(1) plus a month seasonal (production-aligned); energy uses a fuels bridge. A seasonal naïve benchmark has a slightly lower RMSE than the model for headline (0.302 vs 0.318) and for core (0.198 vs 0.214), as already recorded in the backtest report. A quasi-real-time evaluation against Flash releases was also produced (n=10) and was marked in that report as not meaningful because n is below 12; it is not shown. Quality of error statistics: (d).
charts.note: Units are percentage points, month-on-month, not seasonally adjusted. Coverage of 80% uses full-sample error quantiles (informative, not expanding sequential bands), as stated in the backtest report.

blocks.title: Inflation
blocks.read: Services selling-price expectations lead HICP services by 6 months (r=+0.799); excluding 2020–23 the best lag is 10 months (r=+0.636). Industry selling-price expectations lead HICP NEIG by 10 months (r=+0.822); excluding 2020–23 the lead is pandemic-sensitive (k=12, r=+0.308). Extra-EA import prices, CPA B–D, have a measured 9–10 month lead versus NEIG (d). The ECB wage tracker is coincident/diagnostic, not leading: versus HICP services, k=0, r=+0.881, and out of sample it is worse than an AR. October 2026 HICP is the flash; the final is due on 18 November.

charts.title: Selling-price expectations in services: leading indicator
charts.caption: Role: leading. European Commission BCS, services selling-price expectations (next 3 months), euro area (EA21), advanced 6 months versus HICP services inflation (d, full-sample expected-sign best lag). Unit: Balance (SPE); annual % change (HICP services). Source: European Commission BCS via Eurostat; Eurostat HICP; staff calculations (d). As of: 12 Nov 2026, 18:41 Europe/Zurich. Full-sample lead k=6, r=+0.799 (n=277); ex-2020–23: k=10, r=+0.636. OOS RMSE ratios vs an AR of services inflation: 0.850 at 3 months (p=0.008) and 0.770 at 6 months (p=0.039). Services SPE history on EA21 starts April 2003. October 2026 HICP services is the flash (e); the final is due on 18 November. Staff view, not ECB staff projections.

blocks.title: Labour
blocks.read: The Employment Expectations Indicator leads the unemployment rate by 11 months (r=−0.495; excluding 2020–23: 12 months, r=−0.519). Industry employment expectations also lead the unemployment rate by 11 months (r=−0.413). Consumer unemployment expectations are shown at a 12-month lag, the ex-2020–23 best lag (r=+0.520); the full-sample signed best lag is 9 months (r=+0.412). The Indeed Hiring Lab posted-wage tracker is coincident/diagnostic, not leading, and the sample is short.

charts.title: Employment Expectations Indicator: leading indicator
charts.caption: Role: leading. European Commission BCS Employment Expectations Indicator, euro area (EA21), advanced 11 months versus the unemployment rate (d, full-sample expected-sign best lag). Dual axis. Unit: Index (EEI); % of the labour force (unemployment, SA). Source: European Commission BCS via Eurostat; Eurostat labour force; staff calculations (d). As of: 12 Nov 2026, 18:41 Europe/Zurich. Full-sample lead k=11, r=−0.495 (n=321); ex-2020–23: k=12, r=−0.519. OOS RMSE ratios vs an AR of the unemployment rate: 0.756 at 1 month (p=0.002) and 0.679 at 3 months (p=0.044). Versus the 3-month change in unemployment the series is nearly coincident (k=1, r=−0.716). Versus employment y/y (d): coincident, k=0, r=+0.867. Last unemployment observation: September 2026 = 6.5%. Staff view, not ECB staff projections.

charts.title: Consumer unemployment expectations (next 12 months): leading indicator
charts.caption: Role: leading. European Commission BCS consumer unemployment expectations, euro area (EA21), advanced 12 months versus the unemployment rate (d, ex-2020–23 expected-sign best lag). The full-sample signed best lag is 9 months (see footnote). Dual axis. Unit: Balance (UE-NY); % of the labour force (unemployment, SA). Source: European Commission BCS via Eurostat; Eurostat labour force; staff calculations (d). As of: 12 Nov 2026, 18:41 Europe/Zurich. The chart uses k=12, the ex-2020–23 expected-sign best lag (r=+0.520). Full-sample signed best lag is k=9, r=+0.412. OOS RMSE ratios vs an AR of the unemployment rate: 0.852 at 1 month (p=0.072) and 0.867 at 3 months (p=0.331) — a weaker OOS gain than EEI or industry employment expectations, and not statistically significant at conventional levels at h=3. Last unemployment observation: September 2026 = 6.5%. Staff view, not ECB staff projections.

blocks.title: Growth
blocks.read: The AAA 10y–3m yield spread is a recession-risk indicator, not a growth lead. There is no usable linear lead on GDP growth; the sign at lag 0 is wrong (r=−0.145), and out of sample the series is worse than an AR (RMSE ratios 1.10–1.20). A recession probit versus CEPR dates is not yet tested (n/a). BLS credit standards lead real GDP y/y by 3 quarters (r=−0.379; excluding 2020–23: k=2, r=−0.738). ESI is coincident/diagnostic (versus real GDP y/y, k=0, r=+0.782). New CISS has a short 1–2 quarter lead on mean GDP y/y (k=1, r=−0.432; excluding 2020–23: k=2, r=−0.644).

charts.title: Yield curve slope (AAA 10y–3m): recession-risk indicator
charts.caption: Role: recession-risk indicator, not a growth lead. Euro-area AAA 10-year minus 3-month government spot yield (d, inner join, no fill). Monthly average of observed days. Months with a negative monthly average are shaded. GDP is not plotted on this chart. Unit: Percentage points. Source: ECB Data Portal (YC, AAA curve); staff calculations (d). As of: 12 Nov 2026, 18:41 Europe/Zurich. Null result vs mean real GDP y/y (2004-Q4–2026-Q3, d): no usable linear lead; all k=0…6 have r≤0; signed best k=4, r=−0.000; r at lag 0 = −0.145 (wrong sign, n=84). OOS RMSE ratios 1.104–1.198, all worse than an AR. A recession probit versus CEPR dates is not yet tested (n/a). Only inversion in the AAA monthly average: February 2023–December 2024 (minimum −1.566 in January 2024). AAA did not invert in 2008 (monthly-average minimum +0.125, August 2008). Series starts 6 September 2004. Latest: 11 November 2026 = 0.720 pp (10y 3.340, 3m 2.620); November monthly average 0.717 (8 observed days, partial). Staff view, not ECB staff projections.
